page.title: Species recorded on the trails
page.description: 13 plant species recorded on the Corrin Loop and the Old Cattle Trail in August 2026, with the determinations logged for each.

hero.title:
13 species,
recorded on the trails.
hero.intro: Logged on the Corrin Loop and the Old Cattle Trail in August 2026, with a determination for each.

blocks.text: Records made using [Pl@ntNet](https://plantnet.org/). Descriptions are summarised from the [BSBI Plant Atlas 2020](https://plantatlas2020.org/), with the account for each species linked beneath it.

items.name: Bilberry
items.alt: A low bilberry shrub carrying ripe blue-black berries among small oval leaves, open hillside behind
items.description: A low shrub of acid ground that will not grow over lime. It is often dominant alongside heather on well-drained heath and moor, particularly in the uplands, and forms an understorey in birch, pine and oak woodland. It rarely regenerates from seed.

items.name: Common figwort
items.alt: An upright stem carrying small maroon and green figwort flowers above opposite toothed leaves
items.description: A perennial herb that takes either sun or shade and prefers a fertile soil. It grows in damp woodland and along woodland rides, hedgebanks, ditches and riversides, and turns up occasionally on drier waste ground. Mostly a lowland plant.

items.name: Devil's bit Scabious
items.alt: Two rounded flower heads on slender stems, one still in bud and one open to lilac florets
items.description: A perennial herb of damp to moderately free-draining ground, favouring mildly acid soils. It grows in woodland rides, on heath and in grassland, and in fens and mires; in the uplands it also holds on to cliff ledges and ravines.

items.name: Grey Willow
items.alt: Male willow catkins dense with pale yellow stamens on bare spring twigs
items.description: A shrub or small tree of wet ground: wet woodland and carr, marshes and fens, reedbeds, bogs, and the banks of rivers and streams. It also colonises damp waste ground and old pits. Two subspecies occur in Britain and Ireland.

items.name: Heather
items.alt: A spreading mat of heather in flower, fine needle-like leaves on wiry stems
items.description: A low, clump-forming shrub, often the dominant plant on heath, moor and open woodland over acid soils. It takes ground ranging from dry and exposed to wet blanket bog and raised mire. It can colonise newly opened ground such as clearfell in plantations, regenerating from seed long buried in the soil.

items.name: Herb Robert
items.alt: A five-petalled pink flower above deeply divided green leaves
items.description: An annual or biennial herb that tolerates shade and grows on most soils except the strongly acid. Its habitats run from woodland, hedgerows and shaded banks to walls, scree and coastal shingle, and it is very common on waste ground and brickwork in towns.

items.name: Marsh thistle
items.alt: A spiny winged stem carrying clustered purple thistle heads
items.description: A perennial herb that flowers once and then dies, found in mires, fens and marshes, damp grassland and rush pasture, wet woodland, and montane springs and flushes. It spreads only by seed, which can lie in the soil for many years before it germinates.

items.name: Purple moor grass
items.alt: A dense tussock of narrow green grass leaves in open woodland
items.description: A deciduous perennial grass, abundant on wet heath, moorland, blanket bog, mire and fen, and more scattered through open birchwood, montane grassland and stony lake margins. It grows on peats and mineral soils that are wet either permanently or for part of the year.

items.name: Rowan
items.alt: Pinnate rowan leaves with paired toothed leaflets along a reddish stalk
items.description: A small to medium tree of open woodland, cliffs and rocky ground, rocky riversides and moorland. It is widely planted, and birds sow it freely on waste ground and along railways. It avoids dry lime-rich or heavy soils and does not thrive in dense shade.

items.name: Sessile oak
items.alt: An ancient oak with a broad low crown of twisting bare branches on a rocky slope
items.description: A long-lived deciduous tree forming high forest or coppice woodland, usually on well-drained, shallow, moderately to strongly acid soils. It is the characteristic species of upland oakwood. It varies greatly in form, and telling it from pedunculate oak in the field is not always clear-cut.

items.name: Tormentil
items.alt: Small four-petalled yellow flowers scattered through low green foliage
items.description: A perennial herb of more or less acid soils, found in grassland from the lowlands to the mountains, in hay and fen meadows, on moorland and heath, across blanket and raised mire, and along wood borders and hedgebanks. Stock find it unpalatable, and it does not tolerate much shade.

items.name: Water figwort
items.alt: Tall flowering stems of water figwort at the edge of still water
items.description: A partly winter-green perennial herb of water margins: ponds, pits, lakes, rivers, streams and canals, and ditches, marshes, wet meadows, fens and wet woodland. It keeps much closer to water than common figwort, with which it is sometimes confused. Usually a lowland plant.

blocks.heading: About these photographs
blocks.text:
The reference photographs are from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/), under the licence named beneath each one, cropped and resized for this page and served from this site. They show the species, not the individual plant recorded here.

Photographer and licence are shown beneath every photograph, and repeated in full on the [credits page](/credits/).
